items.title: Disney Experiences Showcase at D23 2026: Everything Announced for Disney Parks, Disney Cruise Line, and More (Updating Live!)
items.description: We are here at the Honda Center in Anaheim, California, for Horizons: A Carousel of Progress, also known as D23's Disney Eexperiences Showcase, and we'll be covering all the big news from Disney Parks (Walt Disney World, Disneyland, International Parks!), Disney Cruise Line (Disney Believe!), and much more.
items.author: Adam Bankhurst
items.content:
We are here at the Honda Center in Anaheim, California, for Horizons: A Carousel of Progress, also known as D23's Disney Experiences Showcase, and we'll be covering all the big news from Disney Parks (Walt Disney World, Disneyland, International Parks!), Disney Cruise Line (Disney Believe!), and much more.

We'll be updating this article live as the show goes on, which you can also watch on Disney+ right now!

Disneyland's Avengers Infinity Defense and Stark Flight Lab to Star Actual MCU Stars, Including Robert Downey Jr.'s Iron Man

The upcoming Avengers Infinity Defense at Avengers Campus at Disneyland's Disney California Adventure will officially star some of the biggest names in the MCU, including Robert Downey Jr.'s Iron Man, Chris Hemsworth's Thor, Anthony Mackie's Captain America, Jeremy Renner's Hawkeye, and Iman Vellani's Ms. Marvel.

Avengers Infinity Defense is set to open in 2028 and will see guests helping reassemble the Avengers to battle King Thanos. The journey will take us to locations like Asgard, Wakanda, New York City, and more.

Stark Flight Lab will also be bringing some star power, as it will feature Robert Downey Jr.'s Iron Man, Anthony Mackie's Captain America, and Brie Larson's Captain Marvel. As a reminder, this attraction will set guests in two-person "gyro-kinetic pods" that will roll along a track before getting picked up by a giant robot arm. This will allow guests to feel as though they are flying like an Avenger like Iron Man.

The Avengers and Spider-Man Will Soon Also Call Hong Kong Disneyland and Shanghai Disney Resort Home

Internationally, Avengers Research Testing Labs is under construction at Hong Kong Disneyland Resort. When finished, guests will interact with Stark Industries and other heroes like Peter Parker / Spider-Man. Don't expect everything to go smooth however, as the threat of villains is always present.

Using "120+ feet of storytelling tech," the story will unfold across such locations as Wakanda, Asgard, and more, and there will be plenty of heroes joining you along the way.

For a less thrilling but still awesome adventure, guests will then be able to head over to the Quinjet landing platform to encounter their favorite MCU characters.

At Shanghai Disney Resort, work continues on the fest-ever Spider-Man-theme land and thrill attraction. This section is home to the new Shanghai division of the Worldwide Engineering Brigade (W.E.B. for short!), and it will be where Peter Parker and his friends have created some Spider-Bots to not only help them with experiments, but also build a brand-new coaster.

What's a truly special touch, local artists are being tapped to create more than 20 murals throughout this new land, adding a unique touch to an already intriguing and exciting space. As for how along the team is? The final piece of the attraction's track has officially been installed!

Animal Kingdom's Encanto Attraction Is Called Antonio's Fiesta de Encanto

We learned a lot more about the Encanto attraction headed to the new Tropical Americas area of Walt Disney World's Animal Kingdom, including that it will be called Antonio's Fiesta de Encanto. In this attraction, guests are invited to celebrate Antonio's new gift of the ability to speak to animals.

To help tell the story, the main voice actors from Encanto will be reprising their roles, including Stephanie Beatriz (Mirabel), Jessica Darrow (Luisa), and Diane Guerrero (Isabella).

Disneyland's Coco Attraction Takes Place a Year After the Original and We'll Relive Miguel's Memories of the Land of the Dead

Following the big reveals from Coco 2 and the news that Coco will be a new world in Kingdom Hearts 4, we learned a bit more about the much-anticipated Coco attraction that's headed to Disneyland's Disney California Adventure.

The attraction's stoyline takes place a year after the original film and we'll first enter a "casa museo" that's dedicated to Miguel's great-great grandfather, Héctor Rivera. After that, we'll join Miguel and go on a boat ride through his memories of the Land of the Dead. Oh, it will also have no height requirement.

The Lion King at Disneyland Paris' Disney Adventure World to Feature Simba's Final Confrontation with Scar

The Lion King is finally getting its first Disney Parks attraction at Disneyland Paris' Disney Adventure World, and it will take us on a journey through the tale of the classic film, including the "not-so-happy times."

Alongside a 120-foot-high Pride Rock that will send us soaring down a new flume system with a 52-foot drop, we'll also be witnessing the final confrontation between Simba and Scar.

Carousel of Progress Casts Disney Legend Jamie Lee Curtis and Emmy-Winning Actor Bryan Cranston

Disney Legend Jamie Lee Curtis and Emmy-winning actor Bryan Cranston will voice Mom and Dad in Carousel of Progress at Magic Kingdom 🏰 #D23 #WaltDisneyWorld pic.twitter.com/1MZvwhiUxZ

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

Alongside a glimpse of the new scenes set in the 1980s, it was revealed that Disney Legend Jamie Lee Curtis and Emmy-winning actor Bryan Cranston will be joining the cast as the new version of the attraction's Mom and Dad, respectively.

This is all part of Carousel of Progress' big new update that will send it forward by decades. In late spring 2027, the story will span from the 1960s to the far, far future, and Walt Disney, as an Audio-Animatronics figure, will welcome guests in an all-new introductory scene.

The Yeti Audio-Animatronic Is Coming Back to Life at Animal Kingdom's Expedition Everest

At the showcase, Disney Experiences Chairman Thomas Mazloum revealed that the team is "bringing the Yeti back to life inside Expedition Everest at Disney's Animal Kingdom!" This is a big deal for Disney fans as the original Yeti Audio-Animatronics figure's framing split just a few months after the attraction opened back in 2006.

This has caused the figure to live in its "B-Mode," where it uses a strobe light effect to make it appear as though it was moving. This has lovingly earned the figure the moniker of "Disco Yeti," and it looks like that version will soon be put to rest atop the treacherous mountain.

The Imagineering Season 2 Is Headed to Disney+ in Early 202

Back for more ✨ The Imagineering Story season 2 debuts on @DisneyPlus in 2028 🦾 #D23 pic.twitter.com/W9lMNeT1E9

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

Leslie Iwerks' The Imagineering Story is one of the most beloved documentaries on Disney+, and it was just revealed that we'd be getting a second season in early 2028. The first season focused on the origins of the Imagineers, and these new episodes will follow them as they "help shape one of the most ambitious periods in Disney Experiences history."

Iwerks is also getting ready to release Disney Worldbuilders on August 20 on Disney+, and you can check out our interview with her and thoughts on her Disneyland Handcrafted documentary here.

items.title: 'I Want to Set the Record Straight: That Is Not Happening' — Kingdom Hearts 4 Devs Say KH4 '100%' Will Not Be Delayed Past Late 2027 Launch | D23 2026
items.description: Kingdom Hearts 4 co-director Tai Yasue and series creator Tetsuya Nomura have assured fans that it is a "100% thing" the game will not be delayed past its late 2027 launch window.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Kingdom Hearts 4 co-director Tai Yasue and series creator Tetsuya Nomura have assured fans that it is a "100% thing" the game will not be delayed past its late 2027 launch window.

While the team behind the new Kingdom Hearts game stopped short of sharing a final release date during its big D23 2026 presence, they feel pretty confident the current schedule will stick. Yasue, Nomura, and director of product development at Disney and Pixar games Nana Gadd doubled down on Square Enix's Kingdom Hearts 4 launch plans during a panel at this year's show.

"One last thing I wanted to share: We announced the game is going to be coming in late 2027," Nomura said. "I saw online that some people were saying the release date might still get pushed back. I want to set the record straight: That is not happening. I do hope that people do look forward to the game coming in 2027. A lot of the marketing for the game has only just started, and so I do hope that people also look forward to hearing more news as well."

"There's many things underway, many plans we have underway," he continued. "Now that we are approaching the 25th anniversary, we're thinking about what the 30th anniversary [looks like]."

"I can confidently say and promise that it will launch in 2027," Yasue said. "Schedule-wise, the development is very smooth. It's not like an 80%, 90% – it's a 100% thing. We'll be there in 2027 for sure."

The more skeptical fans believe they have some justification for their delay fears. Mainline entries in the series have suffered infamously long breaks between entries, with the break between Kingdom Hearts 2 and 3 being 13 years. We're now going on eight years since the last game's launch in 2019, but it sounds like the developers at Square Enix are confident the wait won't be too much longer.

Another reason fans are worried about a delay relates to the recent conversation surrounding physical game discs. Sony announced in July that it will no longer support physical releases for new PlayStation games that launch after January 2028. Should Kingdom Hearts 4 be delayed past that date, it would make it the first mainline entry in the series without a physical release, at least on PlayStation 5. For now, however, Square Enix has yet to confirm any other details surrounding its launch.

Kingdom Hearts 4 was formally announced in 2022 and will launch for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PS5, and Xbox Series X | S in late 2027. While we wait to see what other Disney worlds and, hopefully, Final Fantasy characters the team have planned for the fourth games, you can read about the the extended gameplay trailer shown during the panel. You can also catch up on everything announced during the D23 panel right here.

items.title: Kingdom Hearts 4 Gets Extended Gameplay Trailer Featuring Playable Mickey, Donald, and Goofy | D23 2026
items.description: Disney and Square Enix showed up for the Deep Dive into Kingdom Hearts panel at D23 2026 to show off an extended gameplay trailer for Kingdom Hearts 4 that features a first look at a playable King Mickey, Donald, and Goofy.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Disney and Square Enix showed up for the Deep Dive into Kingdom Hearts panel at D23 2026 to show off an extended gameplay trailer for Kingdom Hearts 4 that features a first look at a playable King Mickey, Donald, and Goofy.

No one expected Sora to show up in the world of Pixar's Coco, Keyblade in hand, when the legendary crossover franchise made a surprise appearance during yesterday's Disney Entertainment Showcase. That only made Mickey, Donald, and Goofy showing up as playable characters in today's new four-minute trailer even more of a shock.

Gameplay for Goofy and Donald seems to mostly fall in line with what we've come to expect from Sora. Outside of one segment that saw the two Disney icons sledding through the Underworld, they can be seen using abilities and teaming up to fight off Heartless enemies.

King Mickey, meanwhile, has received some special attention. The first clip shows him walking around from a third-person point of view before switching to origami-like visuals featuring 2D and 3D gameplay. It looks heavily inspired by Nintendo's Paper Mario, though how long all of these sections will be remains to be seen.

Another surprise saved for today's lengthier look at the game is Riku, who shows up in the video's final moments. He doesn't stick around for too long before the video comes to an end, but it looks like he'll be teaming up with Sora for at least part of Kingdom Hearts 4's events.

Elsewhere during the panel, series creator Tetsuya Nomura refuted claims that the game would eventually be delayed outside of its 2027 launch window. It's been a big weekend for Kingdom Hearts fans, as Disney and Square Enix have also confirmed plans to release an anime series based on the franchise at some point in the future.

Kingdom Hearts 4 is still on track to launch in its late 2027 release window for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X | S. While we wait for updates, be sure to check out everything announced from the panel here.

items.title: Tetsuya Nomura Teases Involvement in Kingdom Hearts Anime Series, Tells Fans to Let Their 'Imagination Run Wild' | D23 2026
items.description: Kingdom Hearts creator Tetsuya Nomura has one message for fans when it comes to its mysterious new Disney+ anime series: "Please let your imagination run wild."
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Kingdom Hearts creator Tetsuya Nomura has one message for fans when it comes to its mysterious new Disney+ anime series: "Please let your imagination run wild."

The Square Enix and Final Fantasy veteran shared a message with excited fans on X/Twitter after the crossover series made a surprise appearance at last night's D23 2026 Disney Entertainment Showcase. Its presence came not only with a first look at how the next mainline installment in the franchise will incorporate the world of Pixar's Coco but also a teaser for a new Kingdom Hearts series coming to Disney+.

Unfortunately, the big reveal shared little about how the anime project will actually fit into Kingdom Hearts' infamously tangled timeline. For now, all fans have to go off of are a few words from Disney Kids & Family president Ayo Davis and some ethereal art featuring what appears to be a new Keyblade-wielding character. Where Nomura could have intervened to clear the air, he instead chose to encourage speculation from those who are no doubt already spinning theories.

"Production of a Kingdom Hearts animated series has been confirmed," Nomura's message said (via Google Translate). "I imagine this sudden announcement came as a surprise. You are likely wondering what the series will be about. While I cannot share specific details just yet, I have been holding close consultations with the scenario team—and the art team, when necessary—and we have even created new character designs specifically for this project.

"I cannot say anything more at this moment, but the single piece of key art released serves as a hint. Please let your imagination run wild as you await further updates."

Filling long waits with theories is something Kingdom Hearts fans are especially skilled at. Outside of the odd spinoff project, the franchise has seen long gaps between releases. Kingdom Hearts 3, for example, launched a brutal 13 years after Kingdom Hearts 2. By the time Kingdom Hearts 4 reaches its recently announced 2027 release window, it will have been around eight years since the last numbered entry – and that's if there are no delays.

The Kingdom Hearts anime series, however, doesn't actually have a release date – or even a window – for fans to mark on their calendars. The art only tells viewers that it's "coming soon" to Disney+.

"Kingdom Hearts has captivated gamers everywhere with its unique blend of adventure and imagination," Davis said following the reveal. "There’s something really exciting about taking a world fans have spent years exploring through the games and bringing it to life in a completely new way. And with a creative team that is working closely with the legendary Tetsuya Nomura, our new series will be unmistakably Kingdom Hearts, while giving fans a whole new way to experience the world they love."

It's unclear when we'll learn more about the show, but there is a chance we get some details later today. Disney will soon host its Deep Dive into Kingdom Hearts panel as part of this year's D23. We'll be keeping track of all of the biggest updates here. For more, you can see how Kingdom Hearts 4 reappeared for a Nintendo Direct earlier this year. You can also see why Disney Animation isn't writing off a movie based on the series just yet.

items.title: D23 Deep Dive Into Kingdom Hearts Panel: Everything Announced
items.description: D23, Disney's biggest fan convention, continues with a special panel all about Kingdom Hearts. IGN is on the ground bringing you the biggest news, reveals, and updates from the presentation as it kicks off today, August 15.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
D23, Disney's biggest fan convention, continues with a special panel all about Kingdom Hearts. IGN is on the ground bringing you the biggest news, reveals, and updates from the presentation as it kicks off today, August 15.

Titled ‘DEEP DIVE into KINGDOM HEARTS,’ this panel will stream live starting 4:30 PM PT / 7:30 PM ET / August 16 at 12:30 AM UK Time. You can watch it on IGN's own YouTube channel, which we will embed in this article for your convenience once the show gets started.

Disney said the panel will give fans a "behind-the-scenes look at the making of the games,” with insights from the "creative minds, character voices, and more behind the magic."

Nomura made specific mention of the villains in Kingdom Hearts' world, saying that Maleficent plays a "very important role" in the story of Kingdom Hearts IV'.

Riku was also shown off in the trailer, with Kairi urging Sora to "wake up" in a voiceover once the trailer was over.

Yasue also dove into Mickey's gameplay segment, where he dives into a book and navigates a paper world where he creates origami copies of himself. There are big, small, and even paper-thin Mickeys, and if you throw him, he turns into a paper airplane. "It's sort of a puzzle-based game design," he said.

King Mickey kicked off the event with a voiceover introduction for our host, actor Khleo Thomas, best known for his role in Holes. Thomas excitedly waxed poetic about his love for Kingdom Hearts before introducing the panelists: Director of Product Development at Disney and Pixar Games, Nana Gadd, Co-director of Kingdom Hearts IV, Tai Yasue, and Tetsuya Nomura himself!

"Thank you so much for inviting me today. It's been seeral years, but I finally managed to get myself out here. I actually got here yesterday, but becayuse my apperance was a surprise, I couldn't show up until now.," Nomura said, via a translator.

Nomura admitted that he wants each Kingdom Hearts game to contain "at least one unexpected world, especially those based on live-action films." He also revealed that The Nightmare Before Christmas was an early "must-have" world for Kingdom Hearts 1, with Gadd confirming that The Little Mermaid was also one of their first picks due to providing an underwater level.

"When it comes to worlds ...I typically proioritize the gameplay experience above all else," Nomura continued. "We think about what worlds and which characters would make those the most enjoyable for players. When I do have a chance that we absolutely need to inclued a certain world, I think about how it synergizes overall with Sora's story, and when considering overall themes, we thought Coco would be the best to help us achieve that goal."

items.title: Dave Filoni Confirms Disney Isn't Making Scrapped Star Wars Movie The Hunt for Ben Solo 'Right Now' | D23 2026
items.description: Lucasfilm president Dave Filoni has confirmed that, despite the push from fans, Disney still isn't working on its scrapped Star Wars movie The Hunt for Ben Solo.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Lucasfilm president Dave Filoni has confirmed that, despite the push from fans, Disney still isn't working on its scrapped Star Wars movie The Hunt for Ben Solo.

Variety pressed The Clone Wars orchestrator about the shelved Steven Soderbergh project after last night's Disney Entertainment Showcase at D23 2026. Considering fans have been pushing Disney and Lucasfilm to bring Adam Driver's Kylo Ren back for The Hunt for Ben Solo for months, it shouldn't be a surprise to hear Filoni has been expecting to be asked about the project for some time.

"You know, someone was going to ask me that in this line," he said with a smile. "I'm surprised it took this long, so that's really cool."

Dave Filoni confirms that Lucasfilm is not making “The Hunt for Ben Solo” right now. #D23 pic.twitter.com/pH414RuZtc

— Variety (@Variety) August 15, 2026

Filoni, gesturing with a reference to the Jedi's hand-waving mind tricks, then said, "We're not making that picture right now. That's all I can say."

He had a similar response for Deadline: "It’s not here, you won’t find it here. The force is not with us in that regard; I love the love you feel for it."

Fans perked up with the hope for more sequel trilogy Star Wars when Driver spilled the beans about a shelved project last October. He said the project was in development with the title The Hunt for Ben Solo and had been worked on by he and Soderbergh for two years before Disney pulled the plug. At the time, the Traffic director said, "I really enjoyed making the movie in my head. I’m just sorry the fans won’t get to see it."

Even former Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy said The Hunt for Ben Solo's script was "great," but that didn't stop Disney from setting the film aside. Considering Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker left Kylo Ren's story on a bit of a sour note, intensity from fans has really only ramped up the last few months. While some flew a "Save The Hunt for Ben Solo" banner over Walt Disney Studios, others waited for the premiere of this year's The Mandalorian and Grogu to voice their dissatisfaction.

Although Soderbergh went on to call the move to scrap the movie "insane," adding that Disney got "two and a half years of free work" from him, Driver, and screenwriter Rebecca Blunt, it doesn't sound like he's been hopeful that the project could rematerialize. When asked in April if there was a possibility of The Hunt for Ben Solo being revived, he said, "nope."

"If it was gonna happen, it would have happened," Soderbergh told The Playlist. "It's that simple."

With Filoni now in charge of Lucasfilm, it sounds like that possibility still isn't high, at least not yet. His tongue-in-cheek answer does at least suggest the Star Wars minds at Disney are more than aware that it's something fans want to see, though.

In the meantime, Star Wars is chugging ahead. Following The Mandalorian and Grogu's premiere in May, the franchise is set to continue on Disney+ with Ahsoka Season 2 thanks to its newly revealed January 2027 release date. D23 also gave IGN a sneak peek at the first trailer for 2027's Star Wars: Starfighter. You can catch up on all of the event's biggest announcements right here.

items.title: X-Men Director Teases Comic Book Inspirations and 'Something New' for the MCU After Marvel's Big Cast Reveal | D23 2026
items.description: X-Men director Jake Schreier has teased some of the comic book inspirations for his new MCU reboot, saying that he's already talked to Marvel Studios about finding the "things that haven't recently been done well" in the movies.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
X-Men director Jake Schreier has teased some of the comic book inspirations for his new MCU reboot, saying that he's already talked to Marvel Studios about finding the "things that haven't recently been done well" in the movies.

The filmmaker leading the charge on what seems to be the first post-Avengers: Secret Wars movie spoke about some of the corners of the mutant universe he and MCU boss Kevin Feige have already started digging through during an interview with Good Morning America. The conversation followed the film's explosive D23 2026 X-Men cast reveal, which included announcements for characters like Rogue, Storm, Professor X, and Mister Sinister.

With its May 2028 release still almost two years away, Schreier, who previously helmed Marvel's Thunderbolts*, stopped short of revealing too much about the movie's plot. Instead, his comments suggested fans may want to brush up on the work of comic book authors Chris Claremont and Jonathan Hickman.

"One of the great things about the comics is there is such a rich and broad history," he said. "That was one of the first things that Kevin and I talked about when I came in; they made many great movies in this world, and they've made so many great things. Let's find the things that haven't recently been done well. All these other corners of the universe…"

"Digging back into those comics like 20 years, the whole Chris Claremont run, the newer Jonathan Hickman stuff. There are so many stories that are still untold, to honor and to reach into, and then to meet this cast and try to do something new, I think you always want to see something that reveres where it came from and then is still taking a new spin on where we want to go."

As teased by Feige, Schreier's MCU X-Men team is still coming together, but they've got after last night, it's clear there's already a pretty solid foundation in place. The D23 reveal saw Inde Navarrette confirmed as Rogue, Maya Boyd as Storm, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, and Adam Driver as Mister Sinister. Joining them on stage were a few previously announced parts, including Kit Connor as Cyclops, Samara Weaving as Emma Frost, and Sadie Sink as Jean Grey.

Earlier in the same interview, Connor teased his connection to the X-Men. He also teased a new direction for the mutant superhero group for the 2028 film.

"I grew up with the original movies in a lot of ways, and it's really cool because it also feels like we are doing a really different version, a different take, which is really exciting."

As of last night, X-Men is confirmed to premiere May 5, 2028. Ghost Rider is also due out that year but does not have a date, with Black Panther 3 locked in to arrive December 15, 2028.

Up next on the MCU calendar is VisionQuest in October and Avengers: Doomsday in December, with both receiving new trailers at D23, too. For more, you can read all about the biggest reveals from the show.

items.title: Frozen 3 Footage Teases New Villain, and It Looks Like Olaf is Getting a Love Interest
items.description: Disney has shown off a first look at Frozen 3 at its fan event, D23.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Disney has shown off a first look at Frozen 3 at its fan event, D23.

The section on the company's hugely-anticipated Frozen threequel capped off the evening's festivities, beginning with a rather ominous tune sung by Idina Menzel and Kristen Bell. Next up was a romantic number for Olaf the snowman sung by Josh Gad, before a clip from what looked to be early in the new film that revealed its villain.

Frozen 3 will pick up the action as Anna and Kristoff finally get married, an event which brings the whole gang, including Elsa, Olaf and Sven the reindeer, to get back together. But on the evening of the ceremony, a mysterious curtain of Northern Lights descends upon Arendelle's fjord, heralding the arrival of a new threat.

Lyrics sung by Menzel and Bell describe this moment: "she sends an invitation from the Northern Lights so shining" which is later referred to as a "cursed frozen heart."

"Doesn't it feel like the world of Frozen is a bit different?" Bell said afterwards, before Menzel agreed that their characters were "going on their biggest journey yet."

Of course, the series' humor will not be lost despite a seemingly darker turn. Taking to the stage, Gad sang a funky romantic tune suggesting Olaf will fall in love — with a character named Samantha, a perfect callback to Frozen 2.

After all of that wrapped up, it was time for that Frozen 3 footage, which began with a jagged snowflake fluttering down across Arendelle, until it's stopped by Elsa — frozen into an ice block. Elsa is curious, and as the rest of the gang turn up ("they were doing mouth to mouth stuff!" shouts Olaf of the newly-weds), a glittering frozen walkway appears, stretching into the Northern Lights.

There's some lighter stuff here, as Anna chides Kristoff for not carrying her wedding dress train, and Olaf celebrates catching the bouquet, but quickly Elsa meets a mysterious and threatening figure.

"Look what the Northern Lights dragged in," the figure exclaims, her face left unseen. Dressed in a dark cloak and surrounded by more jagged snowflakes, the character certainly has a malevolent presence. "The famous sisters of Arendelle! We finally meet," the voice says... and that's the end of the trailer.

Frozen 3 is set to launch in theaters on November 24, 2027, eight years on from 2019's Frozen 2, with all of the franchise's core cast returning. Earlier this year, Kristen Bell played down a report that claimed she was set to pocket $60 million for voicing Anna in Frozen 3 and the already-confirmed Frozen 4 — while acknowledging she was still paid "very well" overall for the blockbuster Disney franchise.

From Star Wars to Marvel, Tangled to Kingdom Hearts, catch up on everything announced at D23 2026 right here.

Image credit: Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Disney

items.title: Disney Animation Studios Boss Jared Bush Isn't Ruling Out a Possible Kingdom Hearts Movie
items.description: Jared Bush, chief creative officer of Walt Disney Animation Studios, spoke about the possibility of a Kingdom Hearts feature film, and he didn’t rule out the idea.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Jared Bush, chief creative officer of Walt Disney Animation Studios, spoke about the possibility of a Kingdom Hearts feature film, and he didn’t rule out the idea.

Kingdom Hearts fans are on top of the world after footage of the fourth game was shown off at D23. Sora and the gang are back to fight the heartless, which are wreaking havoc in the Land of the Dead. Coco’s universe is an explorable world in Kingdom Hearts IV, and Sora even gets a keyblade themed after Héctor's Guitar, along with some calavera facepaint to match.

A Kingdom Hearts animated series was also announced at the event, coming to Disney+ on an as-yet undetermined date. With these two big reveals in mind, IGN’s Jeffrey Vega quizzed Walt Disney Animation Studios’ Jared Bush if there’s anything more planned for the Kingdom Hearts world on Disney’s side of things… specifically, a feature-length animated film.

“Are we ever gonna get a Kingdom Hearts movie?” Vega asked, going on to joke that Bush basically has the power to “greenlight” the project.

“Technically, you’re not wrong,” Bush answered. “I’d say, I’m always excited to hear what people are passionate about. And I’d say that we have a very bright future of new projects coming out — different ways of putting material out into the world. So I would just say, nothing is impossible.”

Bush’s response was, as expected, quite reserved, but his open-ended answer leaves no end of possibilities to the imagination. Given all the good news fans just got about the franchise, specifically the animated show, the idea of a full-length CGI movie following Sora’s adventures doesn’t seem so impossible now... especially since Disney recently bragged that Kingdom Hearts is one of its "billion-dollar franchises."

Kingdom Hearts IV is scheduled for release in late 2027. Combat footage from Coco’s section of the game seen at D23 shows Sora using the keyblade as a kind of skateboard as he follows a flying heartless, to which he’s tethered by a glowing chain. Graphically, the game looks absolutely stunning, with the endless city of the dead giving an impressive depth to the environment.

This most recent trailer also showed off Mickey, Goofy, and our iconic king of the underworld, Hades, as well as a few glimpses of some story beats that take place in Quadratum, a realistic city inspired by modern-day Tokyo — an area that was also shown in the game's surprise trailer at the June 2026 Nintendo Direct.

This isn’t the last we’ll see of Kingdom Hearts IV this weekend; the game will also be discussed on August 15 in a panel titled ‘DEEP DIVE into KINGDOM HEARTS at D23,’ streaming at 4.30pm PT / 7.30pm ET / August 16 at 12.30 AM UK time. Disney has confirmed that it will feature a “behind-the-scenes look at the making of the games,” with names like Nana Gadd from Disney & Pixar Games, Tai Yasue from Square Enix, Haley Joel Osment, the voice of Sora, David Gallagher, the voice of Riku, and Renée Johnson, who voices some of the Disney-specific characters.

In the meantime, keep it locked to IGN for more news coming out of D23 this weekend, and check out everything that got announced at the event’s big presentation at the Honda Center on August 14.

items.title: First Trailer for Star Wars: Starfighter Shown at D23 — Here's What We Saw
items.description: Lucasfilm has shown off the debut trailer for Star Wars: Starfighter at the Disney fan event, D23.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Lucasfilm has shown off the debut trailer for Star Wars: Starfighter at the Disney fan event, D23.

The brief first look at the upcoming movie shows Ryan Gosling’s pilot character, now confirmed to be called Kade Auberon, discover a child playing with his decommissioned starfighter inside a garage. There's a reason it was decommissioned, Kade says. We then see Kade fly across a number of otherworldly landscapes, and in classic Star Wars fashion, droids shoot at the ship as Kade’s droid helps him escape.

On stage at D23, director Shawn Levy handed Gosling a new jacket to wear. On the back is the symbol of his character, Kade Auberon, which you can see below.

Starfighter is a standalone Star Wars movie that is neither a prequel nor a sequel, director Shawn Levy has insisted. "It’s a new adventure," he said of the post-Rise of Skywalker film at Star Wars Celebration 2025. "It’s set in a period of time that we haven’t seen explored yet." As part of that, it will not feature any "legacy characters," so don't expect to see Rey Skywalker pop up.

Ryan Gosling stars alongside Amy Adams, Aaron Pierre, Matt Smith, Mia Goth, and Flynn Gray. Star Wars: Starfighter is currently due to launch on May 28, 2027. Catch up on everything announced at D23 2026 right here.

Photo by Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Disney.

items.title: X-Men Cast Confirmed to Include Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Adam Driver as Mister Sinister, Maya Boyd as Storm, and More | D23 2026
items.description: Marvel Studios has confirmed a long list of names for its new MCU X-Men movie reboot, with its cast now including Inde Navarrette, Adam Driver, Maya Boyd, and more.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Marvel Studios has confirmed a long list of names for its new MCU X-Men movie reboot, with its cast now including Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Adam Driver as Mister Sinister, Maya Boyd as Storm, and more.

The comic book movie company confirmed just a portion of the cast at D23 2026. Some of the actors in attendance – such as Kit Connor as Cyclops and Samara Weaving as Emma Frost – were previously announced, but we'll share the full lineup below.

Inde Navarrette – Rogue

Adam Driver – Mister Sinister

Maya Boyd – Storm

Christopher Abbott – Professor X

Sadie Sink – Jean Grey

Kit Connor – Cyclops

Samara Weaving – Emma Frost

There is a lot to unpack here. First off, those rumors that Alien alum Cailee Spaeny would be playing Rogue have been thoroughly debunked, as Obsession breakout Navarrette will be using her power-absorbing abilities in the MCU instead. It may not be the Mystique casting she had hoped for, but she's probably still pretty happy to be on the team.

Driver, meanwhile, has been rumored to be circling a few roles, including the Master of Magnetism himself, Magneto. While some had correctly predicted the Star Wars veteran's role, he's now confirmed to be playing X-Men villain and evil mastermind Mister Sinister.

Navarrette and Driver have garnered quite the reputation on the big screen, Boyd's film resume doesn't seem to be quite as extensive. Her part harnessing the power of Mother Nature as Storm will see her take her biggest part yet, with past projects including 2023 short Deadbeat, as well as some work on Broadway.

Rogue, Mister Sinister, and Storm were the big surprises, but not to be outdone was the announcement that Abbott will lead as X-Men mentor Professor Charles Xavier. The Hollywood Reported had reported that he was in the running to play the mind-reading telepath recently, with his presence at D23 confirming his spot on the team of mutants. Movie fans will recognize him from his parts in projects like Poor Things, Possessor, and It Comes at Night.

Connor and Weaving had been announced in the weeks leading up to tonight's D23 event, so it wasn't much of a surprise to see them take the stage alongside X-Men movie director and Thunderbolts* filmmaker Jake Schreier. Sink is a more interesting case, as those who have [SPOILERS FOR RECENT MCU MOVIES] seen box-office smash Spider-Man: Brand New Day will know that she actually already made her on-screen debut as Jean Grey alongside Spidey star Tom Holland.

Without counting some of the many, many other rumors that have circulated before today, this is our first official look at the X-Men cast. Marvel still has plenty of mutants to pull into the live-action world, though, so while seven confirmed actors feels like a lot, we'll surely only learn about more in the months ahead.

The X-Men are coming to the MCU:

Sadie Sink is Jean Grey
Kit Connor is Cyclops
Christopher Abbott is Professor Charles Xavier
Samara Weaving is Emma Frost
Inde Navarrette is Rogue
Maya Boyd is Storm
Adam Driver is Nathaniel Milbury

Only in theaters May 5, 2028. pic.twitter.com/ZCd4f7I1W7

— Marvel Studios (@MarvelStudios) August 15, 2026

Marvel Studios also took the D23 showcase as an opportunity to confirm its MCU X-Men movie has a release date: May 5, 2028. That makes it the third film officially confirmed for that year, joining Black Panther 3 (December 15) and Ghost Rider (2028). For more, you can read about everything else Disney had to announce at tonights D23 showcase.

Photo by Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Disney.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

media:description.$text:
X-Men Reboot (May 5, 2028)

After months (years) of speculation, Marvel finally announced this project at D23 2026. The new X-Men movie is set to debut in May of 2028 as the first film in the MCU line-up after Secret Wars. With various characters from the Fox X-Men universe showing up in MCU projects, including in Avengers: Doomsday and presumably Avengers: Secret Wars, the general theory is that the events of those films will reboot continuity in some way -- much as it did in the comics version of Secret Wars -- allowing for a fresh start with new actors filling the roles of Professor X, Cyclops, Jean Grey, and the rest. Jake Schreier (Thunderbolts*) will direct the film. But will they actually recast Hugh Jackman's Wolverine!?

As for those new actors, they include: Adam Driver as Mister Sinister, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Kit Connor as Cyclops, Samara Weaving as Emma Frost, Inde Navarrette as Rogue, and Maya Boyd as Storm.

items.title: New Avengers: Doomsday Trailer Shows Doctor Doom Raising an Army of Sentinels
items.description: Marvel Studios has released a new Avengers: Doomsday trailer, showing off Doctor Doom’s true power and his army of Sentinels.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Marvel Studios has released a new Avengers: Doomsday trailer, showing off Doctor Doom’s true power and his army of Sentinels.

The trailer offers a bleak outlook for our heroes, with a tearful Sue Storm bemoaning what Victor has become. Doom, played by Iron Man actor Robert Downey Jr., is clearly out for revenge after what appears to have been the death of his wife and son (or his mother).

Everyone's looking pretty worried about what's happening. We see a battered and bruised Magneto, Gambit, Steve Rogers, and others all with furrowed brows. Doom, Sue states, is "broken."

We then see a destroyed city, with Reed Richards telling Doom he can't believe what he's done. "Victor, did you do this?" Reed asks. "All of you have lived stolen lives," Doom says. "But now you must give them back." Doom leaps out of a window and crashes to the ground below, displaying an immense power of movement. "Answer me Victor, did you do this?!" Reed screams. Thor tries to stop Doom but he is swatted away with ease. Undeterred, Doom raises an army of Sentinels, declaring: "Hell answers to me, for I am Doom."

During's Marvel's segment of Disney's panel at its fan event, D23, Wolverine actor Hugh Jackman appeared on-screen to riff with an off-screen Deadpool's Ryan Reynolds. Jackman asked to join the cast of Avengers: Doomsday, but it's unclear if this is just a joke or if the due are actually in the movie.

Also at D23, we got our first look at Nightcrawler and Mystique's costumes for Avengers: Doomsday, as well as a new poster showing Doctor Doom.

Earlier this month, former Captain America actor Chris Evans said Avengers: Doomsday will be "brutal" for Steve Rogers. Marvel's upcoming blockbuster will see Rogers return to the MCU for the first time in seven years, with Evans once again reunited with the Russo brothers, who previously directed him in Captain America: The Winter Soldier, Captain America: Civil War, Avengers: Infinity War, and Avengers: Endgame.

Steve Rogers was certainly put through the wringer during those films, though his story seemingly gained a happy ending — back in time with his beloved Peggy Carter. Alas, this happy ending now looks likely to be undone.

"The Russos love beating up Steve Rogers," Evans said during an appearance at Boston Fan Expo. "Their favorite thing to do is to just beat the crap out of him. To them that's what makes a hero, and that's someone who gets punched so many times but still gets up.

"They keep finding new ways to kick his butt, but this one was brutal," Evans teased, "and a really, really good examination into his nature and his values. I'll say... it's probably something you haven't seen yet, but you will."

What could be the cause of this fresh heartbreak for Steve Rogers? Well, with the character now revealed to be a father, fans are fearful that something horrible will happen to his child. After all, Doom appears to have an interest in the children of superheroes — we last saw him holding baby Franklin in The Fantastic Four: First Steps' post-credits scene. Children also feature heavily in this latest Avengers: Doomsday trailer.

Would Marvel go so dark as to kill Steve Rogers' child? It sounds unlikely, but there's still a lot we don't know about Avengers: Doomsday's plot. The film's trailers have previously shown two very different looks for Steve Rogers, enough that some fans think the character will appear via two alter egos. But it could just be that we see a slightly aged-up, bearded version of Steve — meaning his child is now older, too.

Whatever's in store, it was clearly interesting enough for Chris Evans to agreed to return after "at least a dozen pitches" for other MCU projects. While we wait for Avengers: Doomsday to premiere on December 18, you can read about the secret message Robert Downey Jr. hid while at San Diego Comic-Con and see how Feige fought back against criticism of Doctor Doom's lack of build-up.

Catch up on everything announced at D23 2026 right here.

items.title: Marvel Studios Reveal Debut VisionQuest Trailer, James Spader's Ultron Shown in Human Form
items.description: Marvel Studios show VisionQuest got its debut trailer at Disney fan event D23, with Kevin Feige taking the stage alongside Vision actor Paul Bettany and Ultron actor James Spader to speak about the Disney+ show.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Marvel Studios show VisionQuest got its debut trailer at Disney fan event D23, with Kevin Feige taking the stage alongside Vision actor Paul Bettany and Ultron actor James Spader to speak about the Disney+ show.

Bettany and Spader showed up for the presentation to give fans a first look ahead of the new Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) show's premiere this fall. As Vision has been absent from the saga for years, VisionQuest teases a story that dives deep into his mind and his dangerous relationship with past Avengers villain Ultron.

"It's been an enormous joy playing the Vision as he's evolved over the years," Bettany said. "He's been an Avenger, a father, a partner to Wanda, and he's helped turn the tide in some fairly enormous battles. He made the ultimate sacrifice and rather inconveniently died several times, which I can tell you is an act that can make long-term financial planning difficult. But I am told that in the Marvel Universe, no one is ever really dead — unless Kevin says they're dead. And even then, I wouldn't really trust him anyway.

"This Vision is beginning to ask a more complicated question: What, or perhaps who, is he? And what is it that makes us actually human? Which brings us to the person you most want beside you during an existential crisis: Ultron. Yes, Ultron is back, and we're going to figure out humanity together. So obviously, that should go extremely well."

WandaVision has remained a favorite Disney+ show among MCU fans since its premiere back in 2021. The first VisionQuest trailer seems to be teasing a post-mortem on that series' catastrophic conclusion, which saw Elizabeth Olsen's Wanda Maximoff duking it out with Kathryn Hahn's Agatha Harkness. With Vision and Wanda's family disbanded as the rest of the superhero universe barrels toward the end of another chapter, it's unclear how it all might tie into this year's Avengers: Doomsday.

"Frankly, I can’t believe it took you so long to turn to me," Spader added. "Everyone knows Ultron has long been fascinated by humanity."

Check out the new poster for VisionQuest, releasing on Disney+ on October 14. #D23 pic.twitter.com/kgVl3cTUq7

— IGN (@IGN) August 15, 2026

items.title: Disney's Live-Action Tangled Remake Sets 2028 Release Date | D23 2026
items.description: Disney has confirmed its live-action Tangled remake now has a 2028 release date.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Disney has confirmed its live-action Tangled remake now has a 2028 release date.

The latest in its long line of real-life reimaginings was scheduled to premiere March 31, 2028, during the company's D23 2026 presentation today. The announcement came with a first look at the film from the cast, which includes Teagan Croft as Rapunzel, Milo Manheim as Flynn Rider, and Kathryn Hahn as Mother Gothel.

The update for Disney's movie calendar won't see the film swing in for another year and a half. Other details for how it will change from the 2010 original Tangled remain to be revealed.

Here's the first look at Kathryn Hahn as Mother Gothel in the live-action Tangled remake. #D23 pic.twitter.com/hoXrCajxcC

— IGN (@IGN) August 15, 2026

Disney has been building toward the release of its Tangled remake for quite some time. However, it wasn't until the success of its live-action Lilo & Stitch movie that the ball really got rolling.

Croft and Manheim boarding as its stars this past January. Following months of fan-casts, the same month also brought the reveal that Kathryn Hahn was in talks to play the villainous Mother Gothel, with her role in the film confirmed in March.

D23 attendees got a first official look at the Tangled cast in costume tonight, but it wasn't the first time fans have seen footage from Disney's shoot in Spain. Last month, behind-the-scenes shots of live-action Rapunzel and Flynn Rider started to leak out onto the internet. Some images also revealed sneak peeks at Patrick and Hugo McPherson as the remake's take on the Stabbington brothers.

Tangled is now set to come down from its tower March 31, 2028. There's still some time to go before that happens, though, giving Disney lots of time to prepare for a premiere that will hopefully fare better than its live-action Moana outing. For more on Disney's big-screen endeavors, you can catch up on everything announced at the D23 2026 showcase.

items.title: Kingdom Hearts 4 Gets New Trailer, Late 2027 Release Window, and a Disney+ Anime Series
items.description: Big Kingdom Hearts news here at D23, with a new trailer for Kingdom Hearts 4, a late 2027 release window, and — surprise! — a Disney+ series.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Big Kingdom Hearts news here at D23, with a new trailer for Kingdom Hearts 4, a late 2027 release window, and — surprise! — a Disney+ anime series.

The new trailer shows the addition of Pixar's Coco. Also at D23, Disney set a November 2029 release for Coco 2.

As for the Kingdom Hearts Disney+ anime, it's developed with creator Tetsuya Nomura and Square Enix, and reimagines the video game franchise with a brand-new story "that will expand on the universe of Kingdom Hearts while celebrating the characters that have captured the hearts of millions of fans around the world."

“Kingdom Hearts has captivated gamers everywhere with its unique blend of adventure and imagination,” said Ayo Davis, president, Disney Kids & Family. “There’s something really exciting about taking a world fans have spent years exploring through the games and bringing it to life in a completely new way. And with a creative team that is working closely with the legendary Tetsuya Nomura, our new series will be unmistakably Kingdom Hearts, while giving fans a whole new way to experience the world they love.”

Tonight's news comes ahead of tomorrow's Kingdom Hearts panel at D23, where Disney is expected to talk about Kingdom Hearts 4. The livestream of the ‘DEEP DIVE into KINGDOM HEARTS panel at D23’ will be available on August 15 at 4.30pm PT / 7.30pm ET / August 16 at 12.30am UK time. Disney said it will offer a “behind-the-scenes look at the making of the games,” but it’s who’s on the panel that has fans excited for what is now expected news on Kingdom Hearts 4.

The panel guests are Nana Gadd from Disney & Pixar Games, Tai Yasue from Square Enix, Haley Joel Osment, who voices Sora, David Gallagher, who voices Riku, and Renée Johnson, who is behind the Disney character voices. With a panel like that (Yasue is believed to be co-director of Kingdom Hearts 4), you’d like to think we’ll get something on the hotly anticipated sequel.

Kingdom Hearts 4 made a surprise appearance at the June 2026 Nintendo Direct to reveal a first look at gameplay years after the game itself was announced. In a separate post, Square Enix confirmed that Kingdom Hearts 4 will launch simultaneously for PC via Epic Games Store and Steam, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X and S, as well as Nintendo Switch 2.

"A new installment in the action role-playing series developed and published by Square Enix, Kingdom Hearts 4 gives fans a look at some of the characters that protagonist Sora will meet in the mysterious city of Quadratum," an official description for the game said. "Sora will once again journey to realms, where new figures cross his path and new powers awaken his next chapter. Kingdom Hearts 4 will be available at launch on Nintendo Switch 2."

Catch up on everything announced at D23 2026 right here.

items.title: The Princess Diaries 3 Is Taking So Long Because Disney Is 'Working So Hard to Get It Right,' Anne Hathaway Says | D23 2026
items.description: Anne Hathaway took the stage at D23 to confirm that work on The Princess Diaries 3 is moving steadily ahead.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Anne Hathaway took the stage at D23 2026 to confirm that work on The Princess Diaries 3 is moving steadily ahead.

The Princess of Genovia herself confirmed the news during this year's show. Progress is slow going for now, but it sounds like she and the rest of the team behind the long-awaited sequel have a good reason for making fans wait.

"Being part of the Disney family also means being part of a legacy studio that deeply values the family audience it makes content for," Hathaway said. "It’s why we are working so hard to get The Princess Diaries 3 right. Thanks for your patience."

It's been 22 years since The Princess Diaries 2: Royal Engagement came to theaters. That means the wait for more has been especially brutal, though it's not been without its updates.

Hathaway previously confirmed plans to return to Genovia as Queen Mia Thermopolis back in 2024. While the late Garry Marshall was responsible for directing the first two films, The Hollywood Reporter reported that Crazy Rich Asians' Adele Lim had stepped in to direct the upcoming third film.

Author Meg Cabot told the site earlier this summer that she had already read a script for The Princess Diaries 3. It's unclear just how far along it is, but it's at least something she's happy with so far.

"I read a script, and it was amazing," Cabot said. "I told them not to send anymore, because I love it so much. They don’t like it when you tell people what’s gonna happen yet. So I was like, 'Better not send me any more scripts!'"

Julie Andrews, meanwhile, confirmed just earlier this week that she has no plans to return for the new movie. It's unclear how the third film may handle her absence.

"I think the absolute truth is that I think I’m really past all that now," she told The Hollywood Reporter. “I’m not completely retired, but it’s a different kind of work that I do these days — [writing] books, and I do a lot of recording of podcasts and voiceovers. But truly, I don’t think I should be a part of it."

While we wait to hear more about Hathaway's involvement in The Princess Diaries 3, you can read IGN's reviews for two of her recent films: The Odyssey and The End of Oak Street. You can also catch up on all of the other big D23 announcements from tonight's event here.

items.title: Star Wars Disney+ Series Ahsoka Season 2 Finally Has a Release Date
items.description: Ahsoka Season 2 premieres January 20, 2027 on Disney+.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Ahsoka Season 2 premieres January 20, 2027 on Disney+.

Confirmation of the release date has emerged from Disney fan event D23, where IGN is reporting live with all the announcements. The debut trailer for Season 2 is below.

Season 2 arrives three-and-a-half years after Ahsoka's first episodes aired back in August 2023. Rosario Dawson reprises her title role, with Season 2 continuing the story of the infamous Jedi and her friends as they counter an invasion by the villainous Grand Admiral Thrawn and investigate a mysterious neighbouring galaxy.

The threat of Thrawn had been intended as a focus in the now-scrapped The Mandalorian Season 4, so it's intriguing to wonder how plans for Ahsoka may have shifted after Lucasfilm decided to make The Mandalorian and Grogu for the big screen instead. Was more of the Thrawn storyline shifted back into Ahsoka?

Season 2 will also see the return of Hayden Christensen in further scenes as Anakin Skywalker, following his Season 1 guest appearance via Star Wars' extradimensional plane, The World Between Worlds. With more Anakin, and more of The World Between Worlds, fans are wondering how Ahsoka might introduce new kinds of storytelling opportunities in future for the franchise.

Disney has scaled back its live-action Star Wars show production over the past couple of years, following a splurge on limited series such as Obi-Wan Kenobi and The Book of Boba Fett, both of which landed to mixed reviews. Neither Skeleton Crew nor The Acolyte made much of an impression either, with no second season planned for either series.

Ahsoka Season 2 will also see Game of Thrones actor Rory McCann take on the role of Baylan Skoll, following the death of Ray Stevenson. Returning cast members include Natasha Liu Bordizzo as Sabine Wren, Mary Elizabeth Winstead as Hera Syndulla, Ivanna Sakhno as Shin Hati, Eman Esfandi as Ezra Bridger, and Lars Mikkelsen as Thrawn.

items.title: The Simpsons: Hit & Run 'Coming Back in Some Form,' Creator Matt Groening Says
items.description: The Simpsons: Hit & Run 'is coming back in some form,' according to series creator Matt Groening.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
The Simpsons: Hit & Run "is coming back in some form," according to series creator Matt Groening.

Yes, at least as far as the mind behind Springfield and the Simpson family is concerned, Vivendi Games and Radical Entertainment's classic 2000s video game spinoff will finally soon let players get behind the wheel again. He shared his comments during a The Simpsons panel at Disney fan event D23 2026, but it sounds like, maybe, he should have pumped the brakes when it came to any announcements for The Simpsons: Hit & Run.

"I think the original game is coming back in some form," Groening said (via Empire).

Just as Groening let it slip that the Grand Theft Auto-inspired game was coming back, current series showrunner Matt Selman stepped in, saying, "…or not." Whoops.

So, is this a premature announcement, or does Groening have it all wrong? It's difficult to say for now, but when the creator of the franchise the game is based on says The Simpsons: Hit & Run is making some sort of return, it's hard not to raise an eyebrow.

The internet felt the same, as social media feeds quickly filled up with joy as it seemed a 23-year drought without the game could soon come to an end. Groening's mentioning of "the original game" suggests players might want to expect something more like a remaster or remake and not a sequel or reboot. It's hard to know exactly what's coming without something a little more concrete, sadly, so until a more official announcement arrives, it's probably best to keep expectations in check.

What a classic! Hopefully it's a remake/remaster for next gen! pic.twitter.com/zZPAWVhNTv

— Andre Saint-Albin (@AndreSaintAlbin) August 14, 2026

The Simpsons: Hit & Run originally launched for the GameCube, PlayStation 2, and original Xbox in 2003, and all these years later, it remains not only as one of the standout games of the generation but one of the more memorable licensed games of all time. With Springfield re-imagined without losing the show's iconic style, GTA-like gameplay, and the series' iconic sense of humor, it's easy to see why fans have clamored to see it return for all these years.

IGN gave the game an 8.1/10 review. We said at the time that, while it's not a perfect game overall, it's still "undeniably the perfect game for Simpsons fans."

Some of the original The Simpsons: Hit & Run developers said they were shocked it had never made a comeback during an interview with MinnMax in 2023. The years have gone by with few updates, but in March of this year, Selman teased that fans should "never say never."

For now, unfortunately, a The Simpsons: Hit & Run remaster/remake has not been officially announced. Until there is hopefully more to share, you can read about how the rebirth of Radical Entertainment got fans excited earlier this year.

Follow along starting at 7pm PT / 10pm ET for all of the latest updates from what's sure to be a massive showcase.

That's a wrap!

As fake snow falls in the Honda Center, Disney's D23 Entertainment Showcase comes to an end. We saw a ton of news, exciting announcements, and reveals like Adam Driver playing Mr. Sinister in the new X-Men movie, a new look at Avengers: Doomsday, a release date for the Tangled live-action movie, and the first look at Frozen 3. Thanks for joining us.

— IGN (@IGN) August 15, 2026

Frozen 3: Kristen Bell and Idina Menzel reveal a look at the new movie.

The stars of the Frozen franchise are here now to promote Frozen 3, coming Fall 2027. Idina Menzel (Elsa) and Kristen Bell (Anna) started off the segment singing before production difficulties scuttled the act.

“The world of Frozen 3 is a bit different," they say. "Maybe more mysterious. It is great to be back in Arendelle. Anna and Elsa are going on their biggest journey yet. Anna is going on her honeymoon. She’s finally getting hitched to her mountain man Kristoff. Love is in the air for everyone. Even Olaf!"

Josh Gad (Olaf) is now joining them on stage for a song-and-dance routine. It looks like Olaf might have a love interest in the new movie: a girl snowman (snow-woman?) named Samantha.

Now we're getting a sneak peek at Frozen 3.

In the clip, we see the Northern lights. A snowflake falls from the sky, which is cloudless. It becomes a butterfly that flies through the town. Elsa picks it up after turning it into a crystal. She’s wearing a beautiful gown. Anna, Kristoff, and crew show up. “Is our wedding being crashed?” They run onto the lake which has opened up a portal into an ice world. The crystal breaks and turns into a butterfly again. It flies up a hill where a purple swarm of butterflies is surrounding a lady. “Look what the northern lights dragged in," says the woman - who seems to possess ice powers like Elsa.

Hailee Steinfeld and Walton Goggins show off Hexed

Hailee Steinfeld and Walton Goggins, stars of the new animated film Hexed, are on stage now. Steinfeld plays Billie, a character who discovers she's a witch but has no knowledge of magic.

“If there’s one thing Disney is known for it’s bringing the magic," Steinfeld says. "In Hexed, we are bringing the witches. Billie discovers she’s a witch and she has no idea of the magic that’s inside. She’s thrust into a magical realm called Hexed, which freaks out her overprotective mother who tries to follow her. Hexed turns out to be a bit more dangerous than you’d expect."

Goggins, in turn, is playing a witch’s favorite companion, a green, three-eyed cat.

Next, we get a sneak peek of Hexed, which also stars Jodie Foster as the Witch Queen, coming to theaters this November.

Clay - New Disney animated film - announced.

"What if the next Disney mentor stunk?’ Bush says. "And he does. His name is Flip, and he’s chosen to be his village’s next great mentor. His student is a literal ball of clay born that very moment named Mushi (Japanese for insect!). Mushi is a being of chaos, Flip has to keep him alive. Kieran Culkin plays Flip."

Clay is slated for a November 2028 release.

Zootopia 3 confirmed.

Zootopia 3 is officially in the works, it was announced at Disney's #D23 Entertainment panel. pic.twitter.com/Xcqp8JiJhz

— IGN (@IGN) August 15, 2026

Jared Bush, the Chief Creative Officer of Walt Disney Animation Studios is on stage now. He says that Zootopia 3, the sequel to one of 2025's biggest movies and Disney's most successful animated movie ever, is a go.

"You can expect to see all the characters you loved in the first 2 films as Zoopia goes to the birds with some feathery fliers," Bush says.

Ryan Gosling's Star Wars: Starfighter character revealed.

Ryan Gosling is now on stage along with Star Wars: Starfighter director Shawn Levy to talk about their new movie, which comes out May 2027 (50 years to the weekend of the debut of the original Star Wars).

Levy says "the story takes place in a period of time that’s never been shown in Star Wars thus far."

"I owe a lot to Disney," Gosling says. "Had they not looked far and wide and come to my hometown I would not be here today. I’m now here 30 years later and I’m back and it’s changing my life again.”

Levy and Gosling go on to confirm the name of Gosling's character in the movie: Kade Auberon.

"Kade is a guy form the wrong side of the galaxy whose fate is intertwined with the fastest starfighter ever built," the duo says.

Next we get a first look at the movie. We see a young kid open up a garage with a decommissioned ship. Cade (Gosling) says there’s a reason it was decommissioned. Then we cut do a montage of big Star Wars action: lasers blasting at the ship and a droid and two people jumping across a chasm.

Lucasfilm has shown off the debut trailer for Star Wars: Starfighter at the Disney fan event. https://t.co/dhRCgAXXMq#D23 pic.twitter.com/1CYYYvA88l

— IGN (@IGN) August 15, 2026

Hayden Christiansen and Rosario Dawson give us a look at Ahsoka Season 2.

Star Wars time! Rosario Dawson, Hayden Christiansen, and Eman Esfandi are here to tease the next season of Ahsoka.

"It’s always an honor to get to play Anakin," Christiansen says. "And in this season he continues to advise Ahsoka. He challenges her and pushes her to answer the toughest question of her life.

"Ezra is back," Esfandi says. "He's home and he’s reunited with his Rebel family. He is fighting for the New Republic against the Imperial remnant.'

Ahsoka Season 2 streams this January on Disney+.

Full X-Men cast revealed!

At #D23 today, Marvel Studios confirmed a long list of names for its new MCU X-Men movie reboot, with its cast now including Inde Navarrette, Adam Driver, Maya Boyd, and more. https://t.co/ztlRAkD63g pic.twitter.com/NzDKKTSBEl

— IGN (@IGN) August 15, 2026

If a new look at Avengers: Doomsday wasn't enough, Sadie Sink is onstage for quite possibly the biggest reveal of the night. She's joined on the stage by Jake Schreier, who looks to be directing the new X-Men movie.

“We will follow [Jean Grey's] story into an all new version of the saga coming to hteaters on May 5 2028!”

We're getting HUGE news about the cast. Sink and Schreier just revealed some major updates in addition to some of the previosuly-revealed cast.

Jean Grey: Sadie Sink

Kit Connor: Cyclops

Professor Charles Xavier: Chrisopher Abbott

Storm: Maya Boyd

Samara Weaving: Emma Frost

Rogue: Inde Navarette

Mr. Sinister: Adam Driver

Adam Driver has been cast as Mister Sinister in the MCU, it was announced during an X-Men segment of the #D23 Entertainment panel. pic.twitter.com/Q4c9UDc49j

— IGN (@IGN) August 15, 2026

It's Doomsday time!

After a teaser video starring Hugh Jackman, Chris Evans, Hayley Atwell and Robert Downey Jr. are on stage to spill details on Avengers: Doomsday.

We're getting a new trailer. We see Dr Doom on a throne with a Sue Storm voieover. We see Ian McKellen's Magneto and Channing Tatum's Gambit. Doom is looking at a photo of his family. We get glimpses Shuri, Shang Chi, and Thor. A ruined city. Mr. Fantastic (Pedro Pascal) asks Doom "Did you do this?” Next, we get shots of various characters: Steve Rogers with the baby, Loku, Shuri, James Marsden's Cyclops. Thor is scrapping with Doom but Doom easily disarms him. Then, we see an army of Sentienels.

Kevin Feige, Paul Bettany, and James Spader Talk VisionQuest

MCU Boss Kein Feige, Paul Betany (Vision), and James Spader (Ultron) just took the stage to talk about the upcoming series VisionQuest, premiering this October on Disney+ and roll a new trailer for the show.

Marvel Studios revealed a VisionQuest trailer at #D23, with James Spader's Ultron shown in human form. https://t.co/kxfhLpM0yW pic.twitter.com/9M5mjOTsFr

— IGN (@IGN) August 15, 2026

“It’s been an enormous joy playing Vision as he’s evolved over the years," Bettany says. "He’s helped turn the tide in some enormous battles. Made the ultimate sacrifice in Infinity War and unfornuately died several times. It made long-term financial planning difficult. I can tell you in the MCU no one is ever really dead. This Vision is beginning to ask complicated questions. What, or perhaps who is he, and what makes us actually human? Which naturally brings us to Ultron. Ultron is back, and apparently we’re gonna figure out humanity together, so obviously tha tshuld go extremely well."

“Frankly I can’t believe it took you so long to turn to me," Spader added. "Everyone knows Ultron has long been fascinated by humanity.”

Jon Favreau introduces Oswald animated miniseries.

MCU and Star Wars mainstay Jon Faveau is is here to introduce Oswald, who he says is "a character Walt Disney created before Mickey Mouse. He lost the rights to Oswald, but ended up making Mickey. Disney got the rights to Oswald back. It’s coming to Disney+ as a three-part miniseries this February."

Favreau says Oswald utilizes hand-drawn 2D animation and that Disney brought a lot of old 2D animators back for the project. The story is set in many historic locations Disney fans will know.

Favreau is also teasing his NatGeo miniseries Lion, which follows a pride over four years; the longest any crew has ever filmed something like that. Favreau says that nothing is staged in the series and that Hans Zimmer is doing the score.

Lion premies August 20 on Disney+

A new look at the upcoming Bluey movie.

Small kids (and parents of small kids) rejoice! A new trailer for the upcoming Bluey movie, premiering in August 2027, just dropped at D23 and you can watch it above.

Tangled live-action movie gets a 2028 release date.

Kathryn Hahn (Agatha All Along) is on stage now to talk Tangled. Hahn will be playing the villainous Mother Gothel in the movie, which now has an official release date: March 31, 2028.

We're also finally getting some first-look footage of the movie. Hahn says they've been filming on location all across Spain and that the movie is "stunning, hillarious, fab, and kind."

Here's the first look at Kathryn Hahn as Mother Gothel in the live-action Tangled remake. #D23 pic.twitter.com/hoXrCajxcC

— IGN (@IGN) August 15, 2026

Ice Age: Boiling Point gets a trailer.

Queen Latifah and Denis Leary are here to give us a new look at the next Ice Age movie.

“Ice Age is back and it’s coming in hot, y’all," Latifah says. The duo revealed that the team is finishing up the movie now, and that "it’s a funny and scary, adventure [that] will be kicked off by Scrat."

Next, we're treated to a trailer showing Scrat and a baby(!) Scrat. As always, the hilarity kicks off with an acorn, which Scrat has shvoed into the ground. Next, he’s trying to catch the acorn in a river of lava. The mammoths are back. Sid the sloth is back as well, along with a bunch of other familiar characters.

Ice Age: Boiling Point hits theaters February 2027.

The Jonas Brothers hype up Camp Rock 3.

Nick, Joe, and Kevin Jonas are now here to promote Camp Rock 3, which just debuted on Disney+. “We are so pumped to be back where it all started," they say. "Back at the camp, back at the lake, back to pretending to know how to canoe. This time, we’re not the new kids. There’s a whole new generation and the chance to go on tour."

Percy Jackson and the Olympians cast teases Season 3

The cast of the Disney+ adaptation of the Percy Jackson book series is here to tease Season 3, which premieres on November 20. We also are getting a look at some new characters including Athena and Hera, who's played by Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. actress Ming Na Wen.

“The family politics are impossible to ignore," Wen says. "This season we are introducing the Hunters of Artemis, powerful new demigods, and a Titan whos been waiting a very long time to make his move.”

Lisa Kudrow and Mira Sorvino give an update on Romy and Michele 2

Romy and Michele's High School Reunion is getting a sequel and stars Lisa Kudrow and Mira Sorvino are here to tell us about the movie.

“Fashion is still our life, and we still own our very own boutique in Beverly Hills," the duo says. "It’s really chic. We’re entering a whole new phase of our lives. We’re thinking maybe its time to find true love. But will we find it? You just have to find out. Maybe we’ll find true love here at D23. Do you now what this means? We’re officially Disney princesses.”

Angel coming to Lilo and Stitch 2, which releases in May 2028.

In a brief update for the upcoming live-action Lilo and Stitch 2, we're informed that Angel (also known as Experiment 624) will be a character in the new movie, which releases in May 2028.

New looks at Ghost Market and Gatto

To round out the Pixar preview, we got new looks at the original films Gatto, debuting in March 2027, and Ghost Market, coming in Spring 2028.

For Ghost Market, we see the movie's protagonist, a content creator named Kyle (he's from Chicago) being chased by a sentient bowl of ramen and chopsticks before stumbling into a mysterious hidden market in the middle of nowhere.

For Gatto, made by the director of of the Pixar film Luca, we're informed that the movie centers on a black cat named Nero who lives in Venice, Italy. Most cats see water as their mortal enemy. Nero is an alley cat whose the top operative for the cat world’s top mob boss. We're treated to an extended clip from the movie involving Nero, some pigeons, and a girl playing a violin.

Kingdom Hearts series greenlit for Disney+.

Kingdom Hearts is getting an anime adaptation. An original series, "inspired by the globally beloved video game franchise, has been greenlit for Disney Channel Disney+ and is being developed in partnership with Tetsuya Nomura and the creative team at SQUARE ENIX. According to Disney, the series "reimagines the iconic adventure with a brand-new story that will expand on the universe of Kingdom Hearts while celebrating the characters that have captured the hearts of millions of fans around the world."

Coco 2 hits theaters in 2029.

Now, Docter is giving an update on the long-awaited Coco sequel. "We are returning to the land of the dead in 2029," Docter says. The directors from original are back to bring this one to life and make it just as good as the first.

Joining Docter on stage is Benjamin Bratt, who voiced Ernesto de la Cruz in the first Coco movie. Bratt confirms that he's reprirsing his role in Coco 2, which picks up a few short years after the original. In the sequel, Miguel is a bit older now. "He’s a teenager, Bratt says. "Still strumming ‘my’ guitar. To many of you, Miguel is a precious little boy who sang a beautiful song and brought harmony back to his family but to some he’s a menace. Ernesto is back for revenge, sending Miguel on an adventure back to the land of the dead."

Bratt also revealed that characters from Coco will be joining Kingdom Hearts IV, launching in late 2027.

Coco 2 comes out November 2029.

Disney and Pixar's Coco will join Kingdom Hearts IV, launching in late 2027! #D23 pic.twitter.com/xBnPjzIxNj

— IGN (@IGN) August 15, 2026

The Incredibles 3 gets an update.

Pixar Chief Creative Office Pete Docter is now on stage to celebrate the animation studio's 40th anniversary and give some new info about The Incredibles 3. Docter is explaining the premise of the movie:

"Supers are officially legal again," Docter says. "With Incredibles 3, it's the kids' turn to take the stage. Violet and Dash are determined to stand on their own and prove they are ready to be real Supers. They have been sneaking out at night to protect the city. They are struggling to contain Jack Jack, whose powers make him even more unpredeictable and dangerous. A new threat is taking a toll on Bob, who is struggling with his relevance in a world of Supers who have outgrown him. Not all Supers are good. In Incredibles 3 the family will face off against a [new] supervillain."

The Incredibles 3 hits theaters in June 2028

A first look at the new Simpsons movie.

Disney President and Cheif Creative Officer Dana Walden just introduced an on-screen appearance by the one and only Bart Simpson, who teased a look at the Simpsons Movie sequel, which doesn't come out until next year.

We're being treated to stroyboard illustrations of Homer trying to catch a home run at a baseball game where (of course), hijinks ensue as he chases the ball through the entire stadium, out into the street as a horde of fans are behind him trying to catch it. They chase it into the Bowlarama and then into an operating room.

The clip is hilarious and full of classic Simpsons gags. It ends with Homer diving into a giant beer container which promtply explodes. He flies back into the stadium, where Bart picks up the ball. D’oh!

Anne Hathaway gives an update on the Princess Diaries 3.

Anne Hathaway is here to give an update on The Princess Diaries 3. The long-awaited sequel is currently in development and looks like it's not coming any time soon.

"Throughout these films we have grown up together and I’m so amazed at how deeply people have held these stories and characters in their hearts," Hathaway says. "I’m here to ask you please never stop reciting your favorite lines to me. I have come to love being told to shut up. Being part of the Disney family also means being part of a legacy studio that deeply vaues the family audience it makes content for. It’s why we are working so hard to get Princes Diaries 3 right. Thanks for your patience."

D23 Hosts take the stage.

Hosts Ke Huy Quan (Loki) and Ginnifer Goodwinn (Zootopia), the hosts for this evening's showcase, have taken the stage. They're joined by Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro, and are setting the stage for all the big announcements to come.

"We have new stories coming, experiences that will take your breath away.," D'Amarao says. "Announcements that will make you lean over and ask person next to you, 'Did you see that?'"

Go Time.

The lights are down and the show is starting. After a glipse of the Doomsday clock, we're being treated to a promo reel and some Disney notables (Robert Downey Jr., Jessie from Toy Story) shushing the crowd and a massive crew of dancers taking the stage, bopping to a mash-up of classic songs like "For the First Time in Forever" from Frozen and "You've Got a Friend in Me" from Toy Story. Good stuff to follow!

We're About to Begin

Attendees are seated in the Honda Center and the show is about to begin. So far, the crowd has been treated to some freebies and a few cosplayers on stage to get everyone excited.

T-minus 45 Minutes Until the Show Begins

Fans have started to file into the Honda Center in Anaheim, California, where Disney's Entertainment Showcase at D23 2026 will take place. We'll be following along throughout the entire preentation with up-to-the-minute news.

Michael Peyton is the Senior Editorial Director of Events & Entertainment at IGN, leading entertainment content and coverage of tentpole events including IGN Live, San Diego Comic Con, gamescom, and IGN Fan Fest. He's spent 20 years working in the games and entertainment industry, and his adventures have taken him everywhere from the Oscars to Japan to Buenos Aires, Argentina. Follow him on Bluesky @MichaelPeyton
